Subject: Post-call: FinCo migration & compatibility evaluation -- next steps

Hi Alicia

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Recap:
- FinCo goals: consolidate inference to a single vendor for self-serve product features, reduce per-token cost ~20%, and ensure >95th percentile latency < 250ms for chat workloads.
- Top concerns: API compatibility with your OpenAI-based SDK, prompt/response diffs, security and audit (SOC2 + KMS), and migration effort for engineers.
- Existing infra: on GCP, some workloads in AWS; primary models are gpt-3.5-class and embeddings for semantic search.

Proposed next steps (suggested timeline):
1) Evaluation plan (this week): we’ll share a short 2-week eval plan that includes: throughput/latency tests, cost estimates, embedding parity checks, and prompt-diff report. (See attached "finco-eval-plan.xlsx".)
2) OpenAI-compatible smoke test (by EOW): we’ll provide an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and a short SDK swap guide so your engineers can run the same positive/negative prompt suite you already have.
3) Security touchpoint (next Tue): loop in FinCo security for SOC2 scope & KMS questions; we’ll provide our audit artifacts and a checklist.
4) Hyperscaler comparison one-pager: quick callout of key differences vs cloud provider-hosted endpoints (latency controls, dedicated pools, rollout policies). Attached: "redwood-vs-hyperscaler-one-pager.pdf".

Can you confirm: 1) who on your engineering team will run the SDK smoke test (name + email), and 2) do you want us to stand up a temporary dedicated pool for the run or use a hosted shared instance?

I’ll loop in Dylan and Dev on the technical plan once I hear who your primary engineer is.

Best,

Marissa Cole

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: FinCo eval - SDK swap + prompt diff plan

Dylan / Dev - loop-in for technical support on FinCo POC. Key items they will need from us:

1) SDK swap examples (minimal):
- Python example:
  # before
  from openai import OpenAI
  client = OpenAI(api_key=ENV)
  client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-3.5-finco", messages=[{"role":"user", "content": prompt}])

  # after
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=ENV)
  client.chat.create(model="gpt-3.5-finco", messages=[{"role":"user", "content": prompt}])

- Node example (short): replace openai.createChatCompletion with redwood.chat.create. We should prepare a tiny code sample repo.

2) Prompt-diff harness: we will accept their CSV of prompts; pipeline should run each prompt against an OpenAI baseline (they already have logs) and our endpoint, capture token usage and top-level latency. Output: CSV + quick notes on any divergent behavior for first 20 prompts.

3) Telemetry & tracing: please enable token-level breakdown for the run and export a short trace so we can show where token time is spent (serve vs kernel).

Can you confirm availability to 1) prep the SDK examples and 2) own the dedicated pool provisioning playbook? I can schedule a 30-min sync with Raj tomorrow at 10am if that works.

Thanks - will forward the attachments and HubSpot updates shortly.

Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
